paper_metadata.title: Development of high-performance quaternary LPSO Mg–Y–Zn–Al alloys by Disintegrated Melt Deposition technique

evidence.quote: new quaternary MgY 1.65Zn0.74Al0.53 and MgY 3.72Zn1.96Al0.45 alloys (wt.%) were syn- thesized employing the Disintegrated Melt Deposition (DMD) casting technique followed by hot extru- sion.

The mechanical properties of monolithic Mg, MgY 2Zn1 (at.%) alloy (identiﬁed in literature as the LPSO-containing formulation with the best combination of strength and ductility), and two other commercially available Al alloys are also included for the purpose of benchmarking.

mechanisms.name: grain-boundary pinning by broken LPSO particles

evidence.quote: the broken down LPSO phases also served as pinning sites to prevent the growth of DRXed grains which further contributed to the effect of grain reﬁnement

mechanisms.name: dislocation motion restriction by dispersed phases

evidence.quote: the presence of well-dispersed LPSO and Mg 4Y2ZnAl3 phases in the Mg matrix causing restriction to the movement of dislocations and the hardening of materials

mechanisms.name: load transfer to harder LPSO phase

evidence.quote: effective load transfer from the Mg matrix to the harder LPSO phase (Young's modulus of LPSO phase reported in recent work to be 102.3 ± 5.5 GPa compared to 49.3 ± 1.2 GPa of Mg)
reﬁned grains triggered by PSN which activated Hall–Petch strengthening
the effect of solid solution strengthening due to the high solubility of Y and Al in Mg as illustrated in the binary Mg–Y and Mg–Al phase diagram
the presence of worked grains with pronounced basal texture (0 0 0 2)//ED unfavorable for slip

mechanisms.name: ductility retention by random-texture DRX grains

evidence.quote: the homogeneous distribution of broken down LPSO and Mg4Y2ZnAl3 phases which generates sufﬁcient DRXed grains with random texture (lesser (0 0 0 2)//ED) favorable for slip

mechanisms.name: surface passivation by Y and Al

evidence.quote: Better ignition performance of Mg–Y–Zn–Al alloys can be thought to be attributed to the synergistic effect of Y and Al in improving the surface passivating ﬁlm responsible for retarding oxidation.
